result.verdict:
NOT worth it — the fusion loses at every one of the 5 regimes, and loses badly at prefill. Decode: 0.987x / 0.975x / 0.960x (T=1/32/256), a 1-4% regression that grows with batch. Prefill: 0.553x at T=2048 and 0.774x at T=8192, i.e. a 1.8x and 1.3x slowdown. There is no regime where it wins.

Why. (1) The traffic prize is tiny for GLM-5.2's shape. 256 experts x 50.33 MB of w13 per expert means any batch with T >= 256 streams the full 12.9 GB weight set, while the 4096-wide intermediate the fusion removes is only rows*16384 bytes. Ceiling on the fusion is +0.03% of traffic at decode_bs1, +0.26% at decode_bs256, +2.0% at prefill_t2048, +7.7% at prefill_t8192. (2) The cost is large and structural: two staged B tiles need 1.5x the SMEM, and on C500's 64 KB the unfused winner BM128/BN128/BK64/s2 requires 98304 B as a fused kernel and fails to compile (verified, OutOfResources, recorded in results JSON under verification.smem_probe). The fused kernel is pushed to a 32x64 or 128x64 tile, runs 1 CTA/SM, and achieves 0.52 TB/s vs the unfused 0.96 TB/s at prefill_t2048 on nearly identical byte counts. n_regs 214 vs 144 (t2048) and 242 vs 90 (t8192), no spills either way. (3) The split-out silu_and_mul is already nearly free in-chain (0.018-0.038 ms at decode, and the chain measures below gemm-alone + act because its input is L2-hot).

Where it would flip: a device with >= ~96 KB SMEM (so two staged B tiles still permit a 128x128 tile), or a model with few experts / a wide intermediate so the activation is a real share of traffic. GLM-5.2 on C500 is the opposite; sglang's choice to keep GEMM1 and act_and_mul as separate launches is correct here and this measurement supports it.

Confidence: results reproduce to 1-2% under a 4-round interleaved A/B/A/B re-measurement (in the JSON under verification.interleaved_rounds). 2593 configs timed, 0 compile failures, both sides tuned independently with the same grid generator plus a top-3 x top-3 joint chain re-check that can only help the baseline.
result.issues:
1. HARDWARE FAULT FOUND AND FIXED (affects the production sglang kernel structure on MACA, not just my fused variant). The straight port faulted at decode_bs256 with "Xnack Error/ATU Fault(0x8), kernelName: moe_gateup_kernel", which disables the entire MACA context and kills the process. It only reproduces under sustained autotune launch rates, never when running each config once in isolation. Cause: sglang relies on token_mask alone to neutralise padded dispatch slots whose offs_token is the out-of-range sentinel num_valid_tokens, but this Triton's pipeliner emits speculative unpredicated prologue loads, so the sentinel row must not even be addressed. Fix in the shared kernel source (both variants): safe_token = tl.where(token_mask, offs_token, 0) used for both the A gather and the C store, plus a 2 MiB trailing pad on the w13 allocation (the same guard sglang exposes as SGLANG_MOE_PADDING) so a speculative B-tile fetch past the last expert lands in mapped memory. Numerics bit-identical before/after. The bench also now runs one regime per subprocess so a fault cannot lose a whole sweep. Other agents porting sglang MoE kernels on this box should apply the same clamp.

2. One bad timing sample, reported not deleted: in the main run's sequential timing block at prefill_t8192, GEMM-alone measured 52.2 ms, larger than the same GEMM inside the unfused chain (38.7 ms) — impossible. The interleaved re-run gives 37.9 ms, consistent with the chain. It was a one-off outlier in a rep=10 block; every other number reproduces. Marked with an asterisk in the log table.

3. CALIBRATION DISCREPANCY worth propagating: achieved HBM bandwidth measured here is ~1.5-1.6 TB/s (decode_bs32 streams a measured 7.86 GB of expert weights in 4.84 ms = 1.62 TB/s; decode_bs1 0.403 GB in 0.281 ms = 1.43 TB/s), not the ~1.05 TB/s the project brief quotes as achievable. These are pure weight-streaming kernels with no reuse, so it is close to a real STREAM figure. Using 1.05 TB/s would under-predict decode MoE GEMM time by ~40%.

4. The "Triton reaches ~50% of vendor BLAS" calibration is a dense-GEMM property, not backend-wide. For this grouped MoE GEMM the unfused Triton kernel reaches 0.93x the vendor path at prefill_t8192 (38.67 vs 36.05 ms) and 2.2x at decode_bs256 (where the vendor path pays 256 kernel launches).

5. Search-space asymmetry, disclosed: the fused side gets a smaller coarse grid (138 vs 187 decode, 45 vs 79 prefill) purely because two staged B tiles need 1.5x the SMEM. That is a genuine cost of the fusion, not an imposed handicap — the SMEM formula was validated exactly against CompiledKernel.metadata.shared, n_failed was 0 in all 25 autotune runs, and the excluded configs were verified to actually fail with OutOfResources.

6. Vendor-BLAS reference excludes the row gather (A rows pre-gathered contiguously outside the timed region), i.e. it is the best case for the vendor path. Stated in the log.

result.verdict: NOT worth it, except at decode_bs1. (a) ATOMIC: the fused atomic merge moves exactly the SAME number of bytes as the unfused chain — it relocates a streaming write+read of a 98 KB/token [T,8,6144] buffer into a read-modify-write of a 12 KB/token [T,6144] buffer. It therefore wins only when `out` is L2-resident (8 MB / 12,288 B per token => T <= 682). Measured: +0.3%/+1.0%/+0.8% at T=1/32/256, and -10%/-13% at T=2048/8192 where out is 24/96 MB and the RMW hits HBM (the same kernel's GEMM goes 7.80->8.80 ms and 19.59->23.10 ms purely from the epilogue flag). Even a FREE merge fusion would only be worth ~6% at prefill_t8192 (0.63 ms merge kernel + ~0.56 ms avoided c3 write out of 20.2 ms), so there is no headroom to recover. sglang keeping FUSE_SUM_ALL_REDUCE behind a flag rather than defaulting it is the right call; I would enable it only for small-batch decode, and for the L2-residency reason rather than the "avoided an intermediate" reason. (b) TOKEN-MAJOR: fastest and most accurate variant at decode_bs1 (1.083x / 1.094x), and it genuinely never materialises [T,8,6144] (45 KB/token of non-weight traffic vs 242 KB). But it destroys the expert deduplication that the sorted_token_ids dispatch exists to provide: it re-reads a full w2[e] (25.17 MB) per (token,expert) pair instead of per distinct expert. Measured 0.645x at T=32, 0.137x at T=256, 0.032x/0.021x at prefill (986 ms vs 20 ms). The "strong in decode, poor in prefill" intuition is too generous — the correct statement is "strong only when T*topk ~= distinct experts", which for GLM-5.2's 256-expert top-8 router means T=1 and nothing else. At T=32 it already loses 1.55x, matching the 6.44 GB / 4.05 GB weight-traffic ratio (256 pairs vs 161 distinct experts) almost exactly. (c) #9 ResAdd2: confirmed nearly free on top of #8 — seeding the atomic accumulator with the residual instead of zeros costs +0.00 to +0.04 ms (one [T,6144] read); the token-major residual load is ~0.001 ms. But #8 does not pay off, so free-on-top-of-nothing. The cheaper production move is folding the residual into moe_sum (ADD_RESIDUAL=True), which needs no GEMM fusion; that 2-kernel baseline gives the same verdict (f9_atomic vs it: 1.003/1.010/1.006/0.902/0.869). ROOT CAUSE for the whole family: the down GEMM at decode is ~100:1 memory bound on streaming w2 (3.8-6.0 GB/layer) and the intermediate this fusion deletes is only 0.1-0.8% of that traffic. There is nothing to win at decode, and at prefill the atomic mechanism costs more than the merge it removes.
result.issues: 1) REJECTED MEASUREMENT (documented in log §8, both values kept in the JSON): the first pass reported f9_atomic at decode_bs32 as 1.568x, driven by a single anomalous timing of the 3-kernel unfused chain (3.900 ms) that the joint tuning search had measured minutes earlier at 2.511 ms with identical configs, and that is internally impossible given unfused8=2.506 ms and resadd-alone=0.0195 ms. I added a `--retime` mode that replays only the winning configs, timing every chain 3x in an interleaved round-robin and keeping the min of medians (applied identically to fused and unfused, so it cannot bias the ratio). The re-timed value is 2.5091 ms, repeatable to 0.00 ms over 3 passes, and f9_atomic drops to 1.011x. All reported numbers are the re-timed ones; originals preserved as first_pass_fused_ms/first_pass_unfused_ms. Every other cell agreed to <0.5%. 2) FAIRNESS CAVEAT, token-major is not literally the same function: with one token per CTA the M-tile is 1 row, so the inner product cannot be a tl.dot over real data. The kernel exposes USE_DOT as a mapping knob (padded tl.dot at M=16 with 15 rows masked, vs a broadcast/reduce GEMV) and the tuner picks; USE_DOT=False won at every regime. This is a different grid/loop order (which the rules permit) but it is not the same source as the expert-major kernel, and I flag it rather than hide it. The atomic variant IS the same kernel with only the epilogue constexpr flipped. 3) SHORTLIST TUNING (to contain a ~4 s/config MACA compile cost): moe_sum(ADD_RESIDUAL=True) and seed(FROM_RESIDUAL=True) were searched over the top-10/top-6 shortlist of their False twin instead of the full grid; the moe_sum one is on the UNFUSED side so it can only hurt the baseline (conservative against my own result). token-major #9 was searched over the top-8 of #8 plus a refine — that IS on the fused side and could under-sell it, but the measured #9-minus-#8 gap of +0.00 to +0.04 ms (exactly one [T,6144] read) shows it did not. 4) TOKEN-MAJOR GRID SHRINKING AT PREFILL: a single launch there is 250-1000 ms, so the coarse grid was probe-shrunk to 9 configs (warmup 1, rep 3) rather than 82. It loses by 64-128x in weight bytes, so this cannot be mistuning — but the prefill token-major numbers are from a coarser search than the decode ones. 5) do_not_specialize was applied to the token-count args (EM, num_valid_tokens, T, token_num, M, Nd) of ALL five kernels. They are used only in comparisons/cdiv, never address arithmetic; without it every regime is a fresh specialization and a fresh 4 s compile of every config. Applied identically to both sides. 6) VENDOR-BLAS LINE READS BACKWARDS vs the calibration note: Triton beats per-expert torch.matmul by 1.6-2.9x at every regime (e.g. 19.59 vs 30.96 ms at t8192). That is not a contradiction — the calibration is for one large dense GEMM, whereas the only vendor expression of a grouped 256-expert MoE GEMM is 256 launches with M=8-256. Triton's grouped kernel reaches 84.2 TF/s at prefill_t8192 against the 106 TF/s the calibration got from a plain Triton GEMM, so the dispatch/gather indirection costs ~20%. 7) UNEXPLAINED, does not affect any ratio: measured weight-stream bandwidth is above the 1.05 TB/s figure I was given — decode_bs32 moves >=4.05 GB of weights in 2.50 ms => >=1.62 TB/s effective. Either the C500's streaming read bandwidth is higher than the calibration assumed, or L2 catches duplicated expert slabs across concurrent CTAs. I did not chase it. 8) bf16 tl.atomic_add works on this backend (probed before building anything), which is what makes strategy (a) viable without an fp32 staging buffer + cast kernel; the cost is precision — atomic rel_err 7-10.5e-3 vs unfused 3.3-4.6e-3 vs token-major 2.1-3.1e-3, all inside the 2e-2 tolerance but the atomic path is measurably the least accurate. 9) All 2906 config trials compiled successfully (n_failed=0 everywhere); the SMEM/accumulator prefilter left no dead configs in the grids.

Sections 5 Results, 6 Correctness, 7, 8 Verdict are literal placeholders <!--RESULTS--> (293), <!--CORRECTNESS--> (299), <!--HALF--> (305), <!--VERDICT--> (311). No speedup, rel_err, timing or config table was ever recorded. Deliverables 3 and 4 unmet while the log claims otherwise; any f11 claim is unsubstantiated.

findings.summary: The token-major variants are a second, structurally distinct kernel with no unfused counterpart, so their only win (decode_bs1) confounds the fusion with a grid-order change.
findings.evidence: moe_down_token_major_kernel is a separate @triton.jit with its own grid (pid -> token,n-block), its own `for kk in range(TOPK)` loop, register accumulator and USE_DOT dot/GEMV switch - not moe_down_kernel with FUSE_MERGE off. No token-major *unfused* baseline (token-major GEMM -> [rows,H] then moe_sum) was built, so f8/f9_token_major are scored against the expert-major chain. From the study's own JSON at decode_bs1: token-major total 0.1413 ms, expert-major GEMM ALONE (unfused_gemm_only_ms) 0.1480 ms, unfused chain 0.1531 ms -> ~0.0067 of the ~0.0118 ms gap (more than half of the reported 1.083x/1.094x) exists before any merge is fused. Rule 1 permits grid/loop-order changes, so concern not fail, but the log attributes the whole win to the fusion.

findings.summary: Headline `speedup` for both #9 variants uses the 3-kernel baseline, inflating the decode_bs1 win by 8x versus the 2-kernel baseline the same script already builds.
findings.evidence: `base = "unfused8" if v.startswith("f8") else "unfused9_3kernel"`. unfused9_3kernel materialises an extra [T,H] tensor (out_u) no downstream consumer needs. Against unfused9_2kernel (moe_sum(ADD_RESIDUAL=True)), f9_atomic at decode_bs1 falls 1.025x -> 1.003x and f9_token_major 1.094x -> 1.070x (my re-run: 1.063x). Disclosed in log 5.3 and the speedup_vs_2kernel field, but the JSON's primary `speedup` key and the log's 5.2 headline table both carry the inflated number.

findings.summary: Sub-1% wins reported to 3 decimals from a min-of-3-medians estimator on a machine that throws 25-320% one-off excursions; min-of-N is downward-biased per chain, overstating by up to 1.7 pp.
findings.evidence: `best[name] = min(best.get(name, float("inf")), t.p50_ms)`. In my 8-pass interleaved re-runs: decode_bs1 unfused8 = 0.4344 ms (+186%) and unfused9_3kernel = 0.6500 ms (+320%) on pass 0; decode_bs32 f8_atomic = 4.8095 ms (+94%) and f9_atomic = 5.1996 ms (+110%) on pass 6 - i.e. excursions hit the fused side too. Reported (min-of-3) vs my median-of-8: f8_token_major decode_bs1 1.0833 -> 1.0661; f9_token_major 1.0935 -> 1.0839; f9_atomic 1.0253 -> 1.0236; f8_atomic 1.0034 -> 1.0034. Also :863 gives token-major chains 1 pass at slow regimes while their baseline gets 3-and-min (asymmetric, but immaterial at 30-50x gaps).

findings.summary: The fused atomic variant is non-deterministic (bf16 tl.atomic_add of 8 contributions) and its recorded rel_err does not reproduce; the determinism cost is not disclosed.
findings.evidence: `tl.atomic_add(c_ptrs, out, mask=c_mask)` accumulates in bf16 in hardware-scheduling order. Re-running decode_bs1 with the recorded winning configs: rel_err f8_atomic = 0.00916701927781105 vs recorded 0.007016176823526621 (+31%), while rel_err unfused8 = 0.0035188067704439163 reproduced bit-exactly, as did every deterministic variant in f06 and f03. No lost updates (a dropped 1-of-8 contribution would show ~1.25e-1; observed 7-10.5e-3 is the bf16 rounding scale), so the kernel is correct - but the recorded rel_err for the four *_atomic rows is one draw, and a consumer needing bitwise-reproducible output cannot use this path. The log discusses precision (5.2) but not determinism.

findings.summary: Log claims 'the prefilters are exact, nothing viable was excluded'; the fused SMEM estimate is over-conservative and did exclude runnable configs - but I ran all of them and none would have helped.
findings.evidence: n_failed=0 proves only that nothing tried failed. The fused estimate num_stages*2*BLOCK_K*(BLOCK_M + 2*BLOCK_N) (glm52/kernels/moe_gateup.py:188-196) makes the fused grid smaller (45 vs 79 prefill, 138 vs 187 decode). I ran every config dropped from the fused grid but kept for the unfused one: prefill_t2048 38 dropped, 6 compile and run, best 32.72 ms vs reported fused winner 25.25 ms; decode_bs256 75 dropped, 14 run, best 10.12 ms vs 8.52 ms. Wording error only - the reported losses are NOT an under-searched-fused-grid artefact.

findings.summary: A corrupt diagnostic survives in the shipped JSON: unfused_gemm_ms (52.217) exceeds unfused_ms (38.668) for a strict superset of the same work.
findings.evidence: My 4-pass interleaved re-run gives GEMM-alone = 38.013 / 38.048 / 37.962 / 38.024 ms. Cause is the sequential single-shot final-timing block at bench_f06_upgate_swiglu.py:376-382. The agent does flag it in LOG-04 6.4 and marks the cell '*', and the headline speedup is unaffected (I reproduce 0.7731x vs reported 0.7740x) - but the bad value sits in the JSON with no in-record annotation, and f06 never adopted the --retime pass that f08f09 added to fix exactly this.

findings.summary: Three auxiliary tuning grids are asymmetric; two of the three disfavour the fused side. Documented, and immaterial in size.
findings.evidence: resadd_kernel (unfused) gets 90 configs while seed_kernel (fused, elemwise_grid(small=True)+torch memset) gets 15; moe_sum (unfused) gets 126 while moe_sum(ADD_RESIDUAL=True) gets a 10-config shortlist; token-major #8 gets 82 while token-major #9 gets an 8-config shortlist (fused side). All disclosed in log section 3. Measured seed cost 0.0143-0.0832 ms against chains of 0.15-23 ms; at decode_bs1 the seed still came out cheaper (0.0143) than the 90-config resadd (0.0154).

findings.summary: Retimed rows carry stale p10/p90 bands from the first pass, so the reported value can sit outside its own recorded uncertainty band.
findings.evidence: retime_regime overwrites fused_ms/unfused_ms/speedup but not fused_p10_p90/unfused_p10_p90. In the shipped JSON, decode_bs32 f8_atomic has fused_ms = 2.4799 with fused_p10_p90 = [2.4845, 2.4906] - the reported number is below its own p10. An auditor using the band as an error bar on the reported number is misled.

findings.summary: The atomic accumulator is never reseeded during the atomic GEMM's solo autotune, so thousands of launches accumulate into out_f. Hygiene only - no measured impact.
findings.evidence: autotune(lambda c: [prob.atomic_fn(c)], cga, ...) and t_atom_only = bench_chain([prob.atomic_fn(...)]) contain no seed_fn. Values stay O(1e3) (no inf/denormals), atomic cost is address- not value-dependent, and validation reseeds first, so nothing measured changes - but atomic_gemm_only_ms was measured on buffer contents that never occur in real use.

findings.summary: The epilogue config the winning chain actually used is not recorded when the joint pass does not improve on coarse/refine, making the run non-reproducible from the record.
findings.evidence: `f_epi, u_epi = None, None` is only overwritten if the joint pass beats the coarse/refine best; unfused_chain then resolves None to e_add_f32/e_add_bf16 internally. The JSON records decode_bs1 unfused_cfg = {..., 'SPLIT_K': 2, 'EPI': null} - a SPLIT_K>1 chain that provably ran an epilogue kernel with the config unrecorded. No fairness impact (both sides share the gap).

findings.summary: The 'fp32 reference' reproduces the kernel's exact rounding recipe, so the eight rel_err = 0.0 entries are agreement, not accuracy. Not the self-comparison the brief warns about.
findings.evidence: reference.py:22-33 replicates both intermediate bf16 rounds that add_rmsnorm.py:125,134 performs (h1 rounded before the sum-of-squares; the normalised value rounded before * w). 8 of 20 recorded f03 checks are exactly 0.0; I reproduced them, and the tensors are independent, so no self-comparison occurred. The check validates conformance to a chosen (sglang) rounding recipe rather than correctness of the recipe. Both sides are checked against it plus an independent bitwise fused-vs-unfused test (bench_f03_resadd_rmsnorm.py:233-235), so the comparison itself is sound.

findings.summary: Construction is fair and the reported losses reproduce exactly; the smaller fused grid is a verified physical SMEM consequence, not a handicap.
findings.evidence: Chain timing correct (unfused passed to bench_chain as one list at :378). Dispatch layout cached at factory time and excluded from both sides; w13 pad allocated for both. Unfused side additionally gets a top-3 x top-3 joint chain re-tune (which can only help the baseline). Fused legitimately skips [rows,4096]; both hand downstream the same [rows,2048] (fused_vs_unfused_rel_err ~5e-3). My interleaved re-run at prefill_t8192: 0.7731x vs reported 0.7740x, rel_err bit-exact. My 113-config sweep of every SMEM-excluded fused config found none faster than the reported fused winner.

findings.summary: The cleanest experiment in the study; the largest claimed win (1.315x) reproduces and its excess over the 1.25x traffic ceiling is explained by measured bandwidth, not fabricated.
findings.evidence: Perfectly symmetric 152/152 coarse grids per side per regime, refine 38-60 each, and the *baseline* gets the extra joint chain re-tune. The fused kernel writes both required outputs, h1 (new residual, add_rmsnorm.py:126) and out (:136), and is bitwise equal to the unfused chain at 4 of 5 regimes. My 6-pass interleaved re-runs: prefill_t8192 1.3177 (reported 1.3153), prefill_t2048 1.2497 (1.2493), decode_bs256 1.0875 (1.0813). The 1.32x > 1.25x ceiling = 25% traffic saving x 5.8% better streaming efficiency (fused 1.300 TB/s vs unfused 1.229 TB/s).

findings.summary: Symmetric grids at every stage and both chains pay the SPLIT_K zeroing plus epilogue identically; the prefill loss was already independently reproduced.
findings.evidence: coarse 98-120 configs on BOTH sides, refine 6-17 each, joint 15 each (tune_fused_joint is absent only where the fused winner had SPLIT_K=1 and therefore has no epilogue kernel to jointly tune - structurally correct). make_fused_chain:209-213 and make_unfused_chain:224-228 both run [acc32.zero_(), gemm, epilogue] when SPLIT_K>1. LOG-10 section 1.1 already reproduced the 0.846x prefill_t8192 loss and falsified the under-tuning hypothesis by forcing the fused side onto the unfused winner's config (18.851 ms, worse).

findings.summary: None of the four classic rigging patterns is present in any completed family: no summed per-kernel timings, no missing downstream output, no asymmetric setup cost, no shared configs, no self-comparing checks.
findings.evidence: Verified individually: chains passed as one list at bench_f06:378, bench_f08f09:691-699/841-853, bench_f03:243-249, bench_f01:373. Fused sides materialise every needed tensor (add_rmsnorm.py:126,136; f08f09 seeding inside the timed chain at bench_f08f09:704-709; oproj_resadd.py:209-213). moe_align_block_size is cached in Problem.layout() and excluded for every variant equally. Every check() targets a separately computed fp32 reference. Where grids are asymmetric they are asymmetric AGAINST the fused side (F7, F9) - the conservative direction.

result.reran: Four independent hardware experiments on CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, all written from scratch against the project's launchers (not by calling the agents' bench drivers). (1) f06 prefill_t8192, 4 interleaved passes of fused / unfused-chain / gemm-only / act-only: speedup 0.7731x vs reported 0.7740x - REPRODUCED; rel_err bit-exact (fused 2.445576246827841e-3, unfused 5.297073163092136e-3); confirmed the recorded unfused_gemm_ms=52.217 is a one-off excursion (true 38.0 ms). (2) f06 SMEM-exclusion sweep, 113 configs: at prefill_t2048 6 of 38 filter-dropped fused configs actually compile (best 32.72 ms vs reported fused winner 25.25 ms); at decode_bs256 14 of 75 (best 10.12 ms vs 8.52 ms) - filter is over-conservative but NO better fused config was missed. (3) f08f09 decode_bs1 / bs32 / bs256, 5-7 chains each, 8 interleaved passes: all 10 speedup rows REPRODUCED (f8_atomic 1.0034/1.0101/1.0076 -> med-of-8 1.0034/1.0104/1.0076; f9_atomic 1.0253/1.0115/1.0085 -> 1.0236/1.0117/1.0090; token_major 1.0833/0.6453/0.137 -> 1.0661/0.6455/0.137); per-chain spread at decode_bs256 was 0.07-0.18% so the sub-1% wins are resolvable; observed 5 excursions of 25-320% across 96 chain measurements; atomic rel_err did NOT reproduce (0.00917 vs recorded 0.00702) while every deterministic chain reproduced bit-exactly. (4) f03 prefill_t8192 / prefill_t2048 / decode_bs256, 6 interleaved passes: 1.3177 / 1.2497 / 1.0875 vs reported 1.3153 / 1.2493 / 1.0813 - REPRODUCED, rel_err and the fused_eq_unfused_bitwise flag reproduced exactly. f01 was not re-run (already independently reproduced in LOG-10 section 1.1, including a falsification test).
result.trustworthy: Trustworthy as reported: (a) f06 up/gate+SwiGLU at all 5 regimes (0.987/0.975/0.960/0.553/0.774x) - I reproduced prefill_t8192 to 0.1% and proved by running all 113 SMEM-excluded configs that the smaller fused grid hides no better mapping; the "loses everywhere" verdict is supported. (b) f03 resadd+rmsnorm at all 5 regimes (1.098/1.107/1.081/1.249/1.315x) - the cleanest experiment in the study: 152/152 symmetric grids, the BASELINE gets the extra joint re-tune, the fused kernel writes both required outputs and is bitwise-equal to the unfused chain at 4 of 5 regimes; the 1.32x that exceeds its own 1.25x traffic ceiling is fully explained by 5.8% better measured streaming bandwidth. (c) f08f09 f8_atomic and f9_atomic at all 5 regimes - the two down-GEMM sides are generated by the SAME function with identical grid sizes (126/126, 28/28, 78/78), the seed kernel is inside the fused chain, and the decode wins reproduce to 0.2%. (d) f08f09 token-major LOSSES (0.645x -> 0.021x) - insensitive to every concern raised. (e) f01 o_proj+resadd at all 5 regimes (0.996/0.999/1.005/0.871/0.846x) - symmetric grids at every stage, both chains pay the SPLIT_K zeroing and epilogue identically, and LOG-10 section 1.1 already reproduced the prefill loss with a falsification test. Overall: the two families I was asked to break survive. No fabricated speedup was found; the asymmetries that do exist run against the fused side, i.e. in the conservative direction.
result.untrustworthy: NOT trustworthy - nothing to trust: (1) f11 lazy pre-norm - log/LOG-07 line 7 claims "numbers filled in below from the completed run" but results/f11_lazy_prenorm.json does not exist and sections 5-8 (Results, Correctness, half-fused variant, Verdict) are unexpanded <!--RESULTS--> / <!--CORRECTNESS--> / <!--HALF--> / <!--VERDICT--> placeholders; no speedup, rel_err or config table was ever recorded. (2) f04f05 norm+router - kernel and bench exist, no results JSON, no log at all. TRUSTWORTHY IN DIRECTION BUT OVERSTATED IN MAGNITUDE: (3) f08f09 f9_atomic and f9_token_major at decode_bs1 - reported 1.025x / 1.094x against the 3-kernel baseline; against the correct 2-kernel baseline the same script already builds, and with median-of-8 instead of min-of-3, they are 1.003x / ~1.065x (an 8x overstatement for f9_atomic). (4) f08f09 f8/f9_token_major at decode_bs1 (1.083x / 1.094x) - more than half of the gap (0.0067 of 0.0118 ms) is the expert-major -> token-major grid change, not the merge fusion, because no token-major unfused counterpart was built. NOT TRUSTWORTHY AS INDIVIDUAL RECORDED FIELDS (conclusions unaffected): results/f06_upgate_swiglu.json prefill_t8192 unfused_gemm_ms = 52.217 (true 38.0); results/f08f09_down_merge_resadd.json *_p10_p90 on every retimed row (stale first-pass values - decode_bs32 f8_atomic reports fused_ms 2.4799 below its own p10 of 2.4845) and rel_err on the four *_atomic rows (non-reproducible: bf16 atomic_add is order-nondeterministic, I measured 0.00917 vs the recorded 0.00702); results/f01_oproj_resadd.json *_cfg.EPI = null where SPLIT_K > 1.
